numberItems.stem: How many braking systems make up an air brake system?
numberItems.explanation: An air brake system is really 3 systems in one: service, parking and emergency; the emergency system uses parts of the other two (p. 5-1).

numberItems.stem: At about what tank pressure does the governor stop the air compressor from pumping (cut-out)?
numberItems.explanation: Cut-out is around 125 psi. 100 psi is cut-in, and 150 psi is where the safety valve opens (pp. 5-1–5-2).

numberItems.stem: After cut-out, at about what tank pressure does the governor let the compressor start pumping again (cut-in)?
numberItems.explanation: Cut-in is around 100 psi. 125 psi is cut-out, and 55 psi belongs to the low-air warning (pp. 5-1, 5-3).

numberItems.stem: The safety valve in the first air tank is usually set to open at what pressure?
numberItems.explanation: The safety valve usually opens at 150 psi to protect the system from too much pressure; 125 psi is governor cut-out and 100 psi is cut-in (pp. 5-1–5-2).

numberItems.stem: The low air pressure warning must come on when tank pressure falls to between which pressures?
numberItems.explanation: A visible warning must come on between 55 and 75 psi. 80–85 psi is the common setting on large buses; 20–45 psi is when spring brakes come on (pp. 5-3–5-4).

numberItems.stem: A manual reset wig wag will not stay up (out of view) until air pressure is above what?
numberItems.explanation: A manual reset wig wag will not stay in the "out of view" position until pressure is above 55 psi (p. 5-3).

numberItems.stem: On large buses, the low air pressure warning commonly comes on at what pressure?
numberItems.explanation: Large buses commonly signal low air at 80–85 psi; 55–75 psi is the general required warning range (p. 5-3).

numberItems.stem: A manual front brake limiting valve with "normal" and "slippery" settings is found on some vehicles made before which year?
numberItems.explanation: Some vehicles made before 1975 have a manual front brake limiting valve; 1997 and 1998 are the ABS dates (pp. 5-4–5-5).

numberItems.stem: An automatic front brake limiting valve gives the front brakes full air only at what application pressure?
numberItems.explanation: Automatic limiting valves reduce front brake air except in very hard braking of 60 psi or more application pressure; the driver cannot control them (p. 5-4).

numberItems.stem: Tractor and straight truck spring brakes come fully on when air pressure drops to what range?
numberItems.explanation: Spring brakes come fully on at 20–45 psi (typically 20–30 psi). 55–75 psi is the low-air warning range, so stop when the warning comes on (pp. 5-3–5-4).

numberItems.stem: Truck tractors with air brakes must have ABS if they were built on or after which date?
numberItems.explanation: Air-brake truck tractors built on or after March 1, 1997 must have ABS; March 1, 1998 is the date for other air-brake vehicles (p. 5-5).

numberItems.stem: Air-brake trucks, buses, trailers and converter dollies (not truck tractors) must have ABS if built on or after which date?
numberItems.explanation: Other air-brake vehicles built on or after March 1, 1998 must have ABS; March 1, 1997 is the date for truck tractors (p. 5-5).
